thread:
maria: quick proposal for canary holdback/backoff policy. goal: automatic, low-risk stops when a rollout meaningfully degrades latency/errors or unexpectedly increases token cost. looking for design + default numbers to ship in console + api.

kevin: sg. do you have a suggested config shape?

maria: sketch below (YAML for API/UI):
```yaml
guards:
  - name: latency_p95_relative
    window: 5m
    comparator: relative
    factor: 1.5    # pause when p95 > 1.5x baseline
    min_requests: 200
    action: staged_holdback
  - name: error_rate
    window: 5m
    threshold_pct: 0.5
    min_requests: 100
    action: staged_holdback
  - name: token_cost_spike
    window: 10m
    comparator: relative
    factor: 2.0
    smoothing: rolling_median_3
    action: staged_holdback
staged_holdback_policy:
  - hold_percent: 50
    duration: 10m
  - hold_percent: 10
    duration: 15m
  - hold_percent: 0
    action: pause_and_notify
```

jordan: couple Qs: how do we compute baseline? last stable version or global model baseline? and p95 over all tenants or per-tenant?

maria: baseline = rolling baseline from last stable model/service config (30d median p95) per-route. we evaluate guards per-route and per-tenant where we have enough traffic; otherwise fall back to route-level.

elaine: token-cost guard is good but billing spikes are noisy (large single long prompts). can we require smoothing + min_request AND trigger only if both cost AND latency regress? otherwise we'll get false positives.

maria: yes — added smoothing + min_requests. also we can support boolean combos e.g., require two guards true within same window before pause (configurable).

samir: what about tiny tenants? min_requests will block them, but they could still see bad UX if we never pause. maybe for <min_requests we do probabilistic sampling or a soft-rampdown instead of full pause (eg cut to 75% -> 50%).

maria: good catch. updated idea: for <min_requests use micro-backoff: one-step hold (75%) for 20m then manual review. also add a min-absolute-error-count (e.g., >=5 errors) to avoid flapping on tiny signals.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Canary rollout started for model: redwood-llm-v2 on route /chat (canary: 5% -> 25%).

kevin: concerned about automatic pause for canaries with A/B tests that intentionally trade latency for cost. need opt-in flags: allow_cost_regression=true for canaries participating in cost experiments. defaults should stay conservative.

maria: agreed — add explicit experiment_mode boolean. default false. for experiment_mode=true we still alert but won't auto-pause; we instead prefer auto-roll-back threshold.

jordan: UX: console should show which guard fired, the metric values, and recommended action (pause / rollback / continue) and allow one-click override with audit log. also telemetry dashboard: 1h/24h comparisons and a small timeseries sparkline in the rollout card.

elaine: +1 on audit log. also surface the reason to SRE on-call and tenant owner via webhook/email if pause occurs.

kevin: one more: we should define backoff schedule that doesn't re-open too fast. propose exponential backoff on re-ramp attempts and cooldown window per-route.

maria: final proposal for ship: conservative defaults (p95 1.5x, error 0.5%, token 2x), min_requests safeguards, staged_holdback policy (50% -> 10% -> pause), micro-backoff for low-volume tenants, experiment_mode override, and console UI for visibility + one-click overrides. i'll open a design doc + api PR with the YAML schema and UI mocks. can we get thumbs for go-ahead? :eyes:

kevin: :thumbsup: please add test vectors + e2e for per-tenant fallbacks.

jordan: :thumbsup: i'll help with dashboard mocks.

elaine: :thumbsup: will add alert routing to oncall playbook.

samir: :thumbsup: will validate interactions with dedicated routing and quotas.
